# Ashlr Stack

> Configure supported services from your terminal or your AI agent. MIT-licensed. Pre-alpha.

This is the repo entry point for agents. The published short index is https://stack.ashlr.ai/llms.txt and the full reference is https://stack.ashlr.ai/llms-full.txt. In this checkout those files are `packages/site/public/llms.txt` and `packages/site/public/llms-full.txt`.

## Part of the Ashlr ecosystem

Stack is one tool in the Ashlr ecosystem. Together these tools aim to be an autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory, chasing open-source RSI (recursive self-improvement). Agents do the work, and the human acts as a passive board member. Stack is the service layer: it turns provider setup into commands an agent can run and parse.

- Phantom (`@ashlr/phantom`, command `phm`): runs the agents that improve these repos, for example `phm improve`.
- [Phantom Secrets](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets) (`phantom`): the vault. Stack stores the secrets you select here.
- [Locus](https://github.com/ashlrai/locus) (`locus`): identity plane. Pins which account a session acts as; `stack exec --as` uses it.
- [Lexicon](https://github.com/ashlrai/lexicon) (`lexicon`): voice lexicon. Keeps dictated names spelled right.
- [Ashlr Markdown](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md) (`mdopener-mcp`): desktop Markdown app with an MCP server.
- [Ashlr plugin](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin) (`ashlr-plugin`): plugin for Claude Code and Codex.
- Ashlr Stack (`stack`): configures services and wires them into agents.

`stack doctor --ecosystem --install` prints install commands for missing tools and runs nothing.

Agents (Phantom and other coding agents) work on this repo through branches and pull requests that merge once required checks pass. Their rules and kept limits are in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack/blob/main/AGENTS.md). Outside contributors, human or agent, follow the same path in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-with-an-agent): fork, install, run the checks, open a PR. The one required check is CI Gate (typecheck, Tier-1 security tests, `bun run check:crypto` and two secret scans), and PRs land through the merge queue. A maintainer or fleet agent turns on auto-merge for a PR from a fork, since that needs write access. A first PR from a fork waits until a maintainer approves its workflow runs. No approving review is required, and the branch need not be up to date with `main`: the merge queue reruns CI Gate on the latest `main` and squash-merges the PR. The full suite runs daily on `main`. The commands are in [Work on this repo](#work-on-this-repo).

## Read-only commands

No account. These print JSON and write nothing. Node.js 20 or newer matches the engines field of the published 0.3.10 packages.

```bash
npx -y -p @ashlr/stack stack providers --json
npx -y -p @ashlr/stack stack recommend "B2B SaaS with auth, AI, and payments" --json
npx -y -p @ashlr/stack stack scan --json
npx -y -p @ashlr/stack stack templates list --json
```

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL stack.ashlr.ai/install.sh | bash
```

Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://stack.ashlr.ai/install.ps1 | iex`

After install, `stack onboard --json` prints a plan and writes nothing. `stack doctor --ecosystem --json` only reports which Ashlr tools are installed.

## MCP server

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add ashlr-stack -- npx -y -p @ashlr/stack -p ashlr-stack-mcp ashlr-stack-mcp
```

Codex:

```bash
codex mcp add ashlr-stack -- npx -y -p @ashlr/stack -p ashlr-stack-mcp ashlr-stack-mcp
```

Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-stack": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "-p", "@ashlr/stack", "-p", "ashlr-stack-mcp", "ashlr-stack-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Do not run `stack add`, `stack apply`, `stack import`, or `stack onboard --apply` until the user names the project and the provider.

## Work on this repo

From a clone of the repo or your fork, on a branch, with git, Bun and Node.js 20 or newer:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile   # again in each new git worktree
bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
bun test packages/core/src/__tests__/security.test.ts packages/core/src/__tests__/secret-redaction.test.ts
bun run check:crypto
bun run lint
```

After the install, the next three lines are what CI Gate runs, apart from its two secret scans over the diff; their local commands are in [Run the gate locally](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#run-the-gate-locally). `scripts/affected-tests origin/main` lists the tests your committed changes select. For a docs change, run `bun run fresh:check`, `HOME=$(mktemp -d) bun test scripts/docs-freshness.test.ts` and the tests that name each doc you changed. After touching a version, command, MCP tool or provider, run `bun run fresh:sync` first. A user-visible change adds a line under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`, mirrored byte for byte to `packages/site/src/data/CHANGELOG.md`. Push your branch with plain `git push`; never run `scripts/publish.sh`, which is the npm release script.
